headline: Central Cascades Wilderness Permit Requirements
reservation: A specific Central Cascades Wilderness Permit is mandatory for many popular day-use and overnight areas, including the Three Sisters and Mt. Jefferson Wilderness, typically from mid-June through September. Reservations must be secured via the official government portal, often months in advance, though a limited number may be released shortly before the date. This system is separate from general forest access passes like the Northwest Forest Pass.

days.title: Cascadia Waterfalls and Blue Basins

stops.name: Sahalie and Koosah Falls
stops.detail: View these thundering volcanic waterfalls via a short, interconnected loop trail along the McKenzie River.

stops.name: Tamolitch Blue Pool
stops.detail: Hike through old lava flows to see the river emerge into a brilliant, sapphire-colored pool.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour total travel; parking near Sahalie is highly congested.
days.note: Blue Pool water temperatures are near freezing year-round; swimming is not advised.

days.title: Volcanic Peaks and Lava Seas

stops.name: Dee Wright Observatory
stops.detail: Climb this basalt structure for 360-degree views of the Three Sisters and Mount Washington.

stops.name: Clear Lake
stops.detail: Witness the 'underwater forest' through exceptionally transparent waters formed by ancient volcanic activity.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 to 2 hours; Highway 242 is narrow with significant switchbacks.
days.note: Highway 242 (McKenzie Pass) is seasonally closed due to snow, typically opening in mid-to-late June.

days.title: Southern Plunges and Hot Springs

stops.name: Salt Creek Falls
stops.detail: Visit Oregon's second-highest waterfall via the accessible viewing platform or the lower trail.

stops.name: McCredie Hot Springs
stops.detail: Relax in natural geothermal pools located along the banks of Salt Creek.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for the drive from Oakridge; conditions vary with mountain weather.
days.note: Hot spring temperatures fluctuate with river levels; check for health advisories before entry.

intel.title: Trailhead Congestion
intel.text: The Tamolitch Blue Pool trailhead often reaches capacity by 10 AM on summer days. Have a backup destination in the Santiam Pass area if parking is unavailable.

intel.title: Digital Dead Zones
intel.text: There is no cell service along most of Highway 126 and Highway 242. Carry paper maps or download offline navigation data for the McKenzie River corridor.

intel.title: Rural Fuel Gaps
intel.text: Gas stations are non-existent between the towns of McKenzie Bridge and Sisters or Oakridge and Crescent Lake. Fill your tank completely before entering the mountain passes.

intel.title: Wilderness Permit Windows
intel.text: Permit checks are strictly enforced at trailheads for the Three Sisters area during summer months. Failure to present a valid reservation for restricted zones can lead to fines.

intel.title: Vehicle Length Limits
intel.text: Vehicles over 35 feet in length are prohibited on the McKenzie Pass (Hwy 242) due to extreme hairpin turns. Check current road maintenance updates before planning transit.

plan.arrival: Collect your rental at EUG airport and drive 90 minutes to Oakridge or McKenzie Bridge to base yourself near the major trailheads.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are fine for main highways, but higher clearance is recommended for Forest Service gravel roads; check for snow tire requirements in late spring.
plan.goldenHour: Dee Wright Observatory provides an unobstructed sunset view over the lava fields, subject to clear mountain skies.
